_intake_note: Verbatim Opus subagent findings, 2026-08-19. Evidence-first inspection of shallow clone. Basis marks preserved. Ledger records derived from this file are in ../records/.
purpose: A natural-language-to-SQL system that routes generation through a formal intermediate language (Domain Relational Calculus) instead of having an LLM emit SQL directly. An LLM translates the question into DRC, then a loop composes relational-algebra operators over the schema's table relations until an SMT solver (cvc5) proves the built relation logically equivalent to the target DRC; SQL is then generated deterministically from the proven operator tree. It ships a second package, bird_benchmark/, that evaluates the planner against BIRD using both cvc5 logical equivalence against a DRC translation of the gold SQL and SQLite execution comparison.

planner_layer.kind: NOT PDDL, NOT a classical search planner, NOT grammar-constrained decoding. It is an LLM-proposes / symbolic-verifier-disposes loop over a closed, typed algebra of relational-algebra operators. No A*/beam/BFS/backtracking; greedy forward chaining, available-relations list only grows (planner.py:419). Only backward-looking move is a 'salvage scan' re-running cvc5 on already-built intermediates when retries are exhausted.
planner_layer.plans_over: DRC relation expressions: state is a list of available DRC relations (seeded one-per-table from CREATE TABLE), actions are 11 typed RA operators (selection, join, projection, cartesian_product, union, difference, division, rename, aggregate, ratio, anti_join), goal is a target DRC produced by the LLM from the question. Goal test = SMT-proved logical equivalence.
planner_layer.constrains_or_checks: BOTH, at three gates: (1) CONSTRAINS at generation — operator selection is a forced Bedrock tool call whose input_schema enums the legal operators (llm_client.py:129-167,267); (2) CONSTRAINS at application — indices range-checked, params type-built, operator self-validates arity/columns/compatibility returning OperatorFailure (planner.py:342-376); (3) CHECKS after — cvc5 decides equivalence after each application, loop terminates only on unsat (planner.py:440-467). The LLM never emits SQL; SQL derives deterministically from the proven tree (main.py:154-183). Rejections from all gates feed back as negative memory.

llm_layer.models: Single configured model: Bedrock 'global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1' via converse(). Bedrock only, no Anthropic API.
llm_layer.role: Four narrow LLM calls, none producing SQL: (a) question->DRC (temp 0.0, ~180-line DRC system prompt); (b) select_operator (forced tool use, temp escalating 0.0+0.2*retry); (c) summarize_relation (cosmetic label); (d) decide_distinct (boolean, defaults False on any error).

interaction_pattern: NL question + CREATE TABLE schema (+ optional BIRD evidence string) -> LLM emits Lisp DRC, parsed + free-variable-validated, auto-repaired (unquantified free vars wrapped in existential) or re-prompted, up to 3 attempts (question_converter.py:60-64,170-190). Extended-DRC LIMIT/ORDER_BY wrappers stripped; inner core DRC is the planner target. Each table becomes a seed DRC relation. plan() tries two degenerate short-circuits, then iterates up to 50 times x 5 retries: LLM proposes operator+inputs+params under forced tool schema -> validated -> applied -> DRC-simplified -> deduplicated -> appended + summarized -> cvc5 equivalence check vs target. Every rejection recorded and replayed into next prompt. On unsat: proven tree -> simplified -> deterministic flat SELECT with DISTINCT/ORDER BY/LIMIT -> SQL simplifier to fixpoint (skipped for UNION/EXCEPT because the simplifier mis-parses set ops in derived tables, main.py:176-183).

evaluation.benchmarks: BIRD-SQL only (dev split 1,534 pairs, 11 DBs; test split rejected by installer; Mini-Dev unsupported out of the box). No Spider, no WikiSQL.
evaluation.metrics: Dual: (1) logical equivalence via cvc5 over generated DRC vs gold DRC (gold SQL translated by the repo's own SQL->DRC converter), nine Verdict values; (2) execution equivalence on BIRD's SQLite snapshot, set_match (BIRD official) + stricter multiset_match recorded separately. Disagreement cells treated as primary diagnostic. Two relaxations: BIRD FKs injected as SMT referential-integrity axioms; projection-tolerance retry truncates generated DRC to gold's arity.
evaluation.reported_results: NOT_ESTABLISHED. README claims 'near-SOTA performance on the BIRD-SQL benchmark suite' (README.md:13) but the repository contains NO accuracy figure, results JSON, manifest, report artifact, or leaderboard comparison anywhere.

key_concepts.definition: First-order set-builder intermediate language {x1..xn | phi} in Lisp S-expressions, the formal meaning representation between question and SQL.
LIMIT/ORDER_BY wrappers strictly outside the set-based core, so row order/count are never part of the equivalence proof.
Typed RA operator tree over table leaves, each node carrying its DRC and columns; the only thing SQL is generated from.
Terminate when cvc5 returns unsat for (not (forall (rv...) (= C_built C_target))).
Each table predicate is an uninterpreted Bool SMT function, so the proof ranges over every possible database state.
Per-iteration typed list of failed proposals replayed into the next prompt under a DO NOT repeat instruction.
On retry exhaustion, previously built intermediates of matching arity/kind are re-submitted to cvc5.
Three cvc5 quantifier-instantiation profiles run concurrently; first decisive answer wins.
BIRD's declared FKs rendered as SMT forall/implies/exists assertions prepended to the equivalence script.
Every BIRD case carries a proof verdict (all DB states) and an observation (execution on the snapshot); disagreement is the diagnostic.
Operator-curated Test_Case_IDs reclassified as expected_fail, with stale-entry detection.

claims_selected.claim: The emitted SQL is the SQL whose DRC the planner proved equivalent to the target — 'unsat or nothing'.

Contradicted by code: when cvc5 returns indeterminate the node is stashed in best_indeterminate_node and on retry-exhaustion/max-iterations returned as PlannerSuccess, so main.py emits SQL for a relation never proved equivalent.
The LLM never generates SQL anywhere in the pipeline.
claims_selected.evidence: main.py:154-183; llm_client.py all four entry points

claims_selected.claim: No search over plan space: greedy forward chaining, no backtracking, no heuristic.
Equivalence proof covers set membership only; row order and count excluded by design.
Aggregate equivalence is syntactic function-name match + SMT over the underlying condition, not semantic aggregation modelling.
Near-SOTA claim unsupported in-repo: no number committed anywhere.
BIRD 'equivalent' verdict is weaker than unconditional equivalence: proved under injected FK axioms, plus projection-tolerance retry.
Operator choice constrained at generation time by forced tool call with enum schema.
Eleventh operator 'ratio' is LLM-selectable but undocumented in README's operator table.
DISTINCT decision silently defaults to False on infra failure, degrading correctness without surfacing an error.

maturity.kind: Sample by publication (aws-samples, 'sample-' prefix, v0.1.0) but framework-scale by content: 42,526 Python lines across two installable packages with CLIs, documented library API, evaluation harness with resume/manifest/expected-fail machinery.
maturity.tests: 723 test functions (README claims 747 collected), 16,718 test lines — more than the 15,824-line planner package. LLM and cvc5 mocked, fully offline. tests/integration, tests/properties, tests/strategies are empty scaffolding. Coverage targets the risky seams: SMT preprocessing, sort unification, FK axioms, projection tolerance, negative memory, equivalence strategies.

resonances: Typed KG: NOT_ESTABLISHED as a graph; nearest analogue is a typed closed algebra (11 operator kinds, typed DRC AST) plus schema lifted into typed facts (per-position sort unification; FKs as first-class SMT axioms). Schema-validated generation: STRONG at two layers — DRC output parsed/semantically validated/auto-repaired-or-reprompted; operator choice made unproducible outside the algebra by forced tool schema, then re-validated before mutating state. Repair-over-reject is explicit ('rather than burning a retry'). Planning gates before expensive generation: PARTIAL and INVERTED — cheap gates short-circuit the SMT solve, but the scarce resource being protected is the SOLVER, not the LLM; the code states 'still cheap relative to the LLM calls' (equivalence_checker.py:176-178), the reverse of the usual LLM-pipeline cost model. Grounded audit trails: STRONG and arguably most transferable — every intermediate human-readable and printed (target DRC in Lisp + Unicode, relations with LLM one-liners, operator selections with reasoning, full SMT-LIB script per check with verdict, SQL before/after simplification); proof scripts carry lhs/rhs labels so generated-vs-gold is readable post-hoc; BIRD harness emits one markdown transcript per case. Closed loops: STRONG on rejection (typed RejectedProposal replayed as negative memory), weak on promotion (only final unsat promotes), and entirely WITHIN-RUN — rejected_proposals reset per iteration, nothing persists for later runs, no cross-run learning; the operator-curated expected-fail list is the only durable accept/reject artifact.
